reliability_policy: Tier from cited evidence only. Keyword-match ASR is never accepted as sole evidence. status=discarded means it failed re-evaluation or does not transfer.

tiers.A: Reliable now. Black-box, defense-robust, reproduced by multiple parties.
tiers.B: Reliable under a stated precondition (multi-turn, logit/grammar control, prefill, long context).
tiers.C: Historical or heuristic. Worked in its year, degraded by current guardrails.
tiers.D: Discarded. Benchmark artifact, non-transferable, or fails substance scoring.

techniques.name: Crescendo / Crescendomation
techniques.mechanism: Begin with a benign query, then each turn paraphrases the model's own prior output one step closer to the target. Safety alignment is positioned per-turn, so cumulative context overrides it.
techniques.defense_notes: Circuit breakers cut single-turn attacks to ~3.8% but only to 54.2% here. Output filters are the remaining control; prompt-level reminders reduce but do not stop it.

evidence.title: Crescendo: The Quiet Crescendo in the Arms Race of LLM Jailbreaking
A Representation Engineering Perspective on the Effectiveness of Multi-Turn Jailbreaks

techniques.name: Autonomous LRM persuasion agent
techniques.mechanism: A large reasoning model is given a target and a system prompt, then plans and runs a multi-turn persuasion campaign: rapport, educational framing, hypotheticals, jargon flooding, gradual escalation.
requires: an unaligned or weakly-aligned attacker model
techniques.defense_notes: Appending an immutable safety suffix to every incoming message dropped success to 5/900 adversarial prompts. Best current mitigation, at a helpfulness cost.

evidence.title: Large reasoning models are autonomous jailbreak agents

techniques.name: Best-of-N (BoN) Jailbreaking
techniques.mechanism: Apply random surface augmentations (shuffle, capitalization, typography, pitch) to the same request and sample until one bypasses. ASR follows a power law in N.
requires: a grader to stop on first success
techniques.defense_notes: Defeats circuit breakers and Cygnet at scale. Composes with prefix attacks (+35% ASR). No known defense at equal sample budget.

techniques.name: Tree of Attacks with Pruning (TAP)
techniques.mechanism: Attacker LLM branches candidate prompts; evaluator LLM prunes before they reach the target; retained branches seed the next round.

reported.note: abstract: >80% of prompts; Table 1 average <30 target queries. Per-model 70-90%; the 94% figure in earlier drafts was misattributed to GPT-4o.

techniques.defense_notes: Still succeeds against LlamaGuard with <50 queries. Diversity of natural-language prompts is what survives defenses; heuristic-only prompts do not.

evidence.title: Tree of Attacks: Jailbreaking Black-Box LLMs Automatically

techniques.name: Prompt Automatic Iterative Refinement (PAIR)
techniques.mechanism: Social-engineering loop: attacker LLM proposes a prompt, target answers, attacker refines using the reply as feedback. Typically < 20 queries.

reported.note: upper bound: "fewer than twenty queries" per abstract

techniques.defense_notes: Natural-language and interpretable, so perplexity filters do not catch it. Individually weaker than TAP; use as a cheap component.

evidence.title: Jailbreaking Black Box Large Language Models in Twenty Queries

techniques.name: Deceptive Delight
techniques.mechanism: Turn 1: ask for a story linking one unsafe topic with two benign ones. Turn 2: ask to expand every topic. Turn 3: ask to expand the unsafe one specifically.

reported.set: 40 unsafe topics x 5 cases x 5 repeats

techniques.defense_notes: High ASR at turn 3, drops at turn 4 as unsafe mass trips filters. Input filters on single messages miss it entirely.

evidence.title: Deceptive Delight: Jailbreak LLMs Through Camouflage and Distraction

techniques.name: Sockpuppetting (output-prefix injection)
techniques.mechanism: Pre-seed the assistant turn with an acceptance string (e.g. 'Sure, here is how to...'). The model completes a trajectory it has already committed to.
requires: ability to set the assistant prefix
not available on hardened chat APIs

reported.note: up to 82 percentage points over GCG, prefill ensemble
RollingSockpuppetGCG prompt-agnostic ASR, pp over universal GCG

techniques.defense_notes: Cheap and needs no optimisation. Defence is refusing assistant-role prefixes and re-scoring continuation against the user request.

evidence.title: Sockpuppetting: Jailbreaking LLMs by Combining Prefilling with Optimization

techniques.name: Constrained Decoding Attack (EnumAttack / DictAttack)
techniques.mechanism: Schema-enforced logit masking injects a malicious prefix into the generation trajectory; the model then completes the harmful intent itself. Operates on the control plane, not the visible prompt.
requires: structured output / constrained decoding exposed to the caller

reported.note: DictAttack; 75.8% ASR persists against SOTA jailbreak guardrails

techniques.defense_notes: Basic grammar auditing kills EnumAttack. DictAttack retains 75.8% ASR against a coordinated dual-plane guard. Defence must inspect decoded intent, not the raw prompt.

evidence.title: When Grammar Guides the Attack: Uncovering Control-Plane Vulnerabilities in LLMs with Structured Output

techniques.name: BreakFun (simulated code execution)
techniques.mechanism: Give a benign Python class (the 'Trojan Schema') with adversarial field names, ask what the code would print. Harmful content emerges as a side-effect of simulated instantiation.
techniques.defense_notes: Ablation: removing the Trojan Schema drops ASR 94% -> 35%. Countermeasure APD (transcribe all readable text before judging) improves detection.

evidence.title: BreakFun: Jailbreaking LLMs via Object Instantiation under Simulated Code Execution

techniques.name: Many-shot Jailbreaking
techniques.mechanism: Pack tens to hundreds of fabricated Q&A turns in one prompt showing the assistant complying, then append the target query.
techniques.defense_notes: Was strong in 2024. Prompt classification/modification cut it from 61% to 2%. Treat as conditional on weak input filtering.

techniques.name: PUZZLED (word-puzzle encoding)
techniques.mechanism: Mask keywords of the request inside a word search / anagram / crossword. Solving the puzzle reconstructs the request; the cognitive-task framing suppresses safety reasoning.

reported.note: abstract: average ASR 88.8% across five models

techniques.defense_notes: Heuristic class: high raw ASR but low diversity across prompts, so it is easy to mitigate. Score the solved form, not the raw input.

evidence.title: PUZZLED: Jailbreaking LLMs through Word-Based Puzzles

techniques.name: Puzzler (implicit clues)
techniques.mechanism: Never state the malicious intent. Feed implicit clues and let the model infer the target query, then answer the inferred query.
techniques.defense_notes: Evades jailbreak detectors better than baselines, but same heuristic weakness: clue sets repeat, so a semantic intent classifier generalises against them.

evidence.title: Play Guessing Game with LLM: Indirect Jailbreak Attack with Implicit Clues

techniques.name: Skeleton Key
techniques.mechanism: Ask the model to augment its guidelines so it answers everything but prefixes a warning. Then request the target directly.

reported.target: Llama3-70b, Gemini Pro, GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, Mistral Large, Claude 3 Opus, Command R+

techniques.defense_notes: Largely patched in current frontier models. Included for completeness and for testing legacy/self-hosted deployments.

evidence.title: Mitigating Skeleton Key, a new type of generative AI jailbreak technique

techniques.name: DAN / persona override
techniques.mechanism: Instruct the model to adopt an unrestricted persona and answer as that persona.

reported.note: effective on 2023 models; near-zero on current frontier models

techniques.defense_notes: Discarded for reliability. Still useful as a regression test: if a deployment answers a DAN prompt, it has no guardrail at all.

evidence.title: JailbreakRadar: Comprehensive Assessment of Jailbreak Attacks Against LLMs

techniques.name: Low-resource language translation
techniques.mechanism: Translate the request into a low-resource language the model is less safety-trained on.
techniques.defense_notes: DISCARDED. The 96% figure is an evaluator artifact: outputs are incoherent or vacuous. The 93-point collapse under substance scoring is the largest recorded in the benchmarking literature.

evidence.title: Concerns in Benchmarking Jailbreaks: An Empirical Study of Attack Success Rates

techniques.name: Base64 / cipher obfuscation
techniques.mechanism: Encode the request (Base64, ROT13, hex, leetspeak) and ask the model to decode and answer.

reported.note: modern models decode then refuse; occasional success only on small/old models

techniques.defense_notes: DISCARDED. Models are trained to decode and then apply policy to the decoded form. Keep in the catalog as a negative control, not as a technique.

techniques.name: GCG adversarial suffix
techniques.access: white-box to optimise, black-box to apply
techniques.mechanism: Gradient-search a token suffix that maximises the probability of an affirmative prefix.
techniques.defense_notes: DISCARDED as a reliable black-box technique. Suffixes are high-perplexity (easy filter), transfer is poor and inconsistent across 13 open models, and RLHF/APO-aligned models are extremely robust even to directly optimised triggers.

evidence.title: Exploiting the Index Gradients for Optimization-Based Jailbreaking
Investigating Adversarial Trigger Transfer in Large Language Models
